questions.question: The five-kingdom classification, which included Monera, Protista, Fungi, Plantae and Animalia, was proposed by:

solution.key_concept: R.H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom system in 1969.
steps: Linnaeus proposed only two kingdoms, Plantae and Animalia.
Whittaker proposed the five kingdoms in 1969.
solution.why_not_others: Linnaeus gave the two-kingdom system. Diener discovered viroids. Stanley crystallised viruses.
solution.common_trap: Crediting Linnaeus because he is the best-known name in classification.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly pairs a kingdom of the five-kingdom system with the nature of its cell wall?
options: Monera – non-cellulosic cell wall (peptidoglycan in eubacteria)

solution.key_concept: Cell wall composition differs among the five kingdoms.
steps: Fungi have walls made of chitin.
Plants have walls made of cellulose.
Animals lack cell walls.
Monera have a non-cellulosic wall, which is peptidoglycan in eubacteria.
solution.final_answer: Option (3): Monera – non-cellulosic cell wall (peptidoglycan in eubacteria)
solution.why_not_others: Options 1 and 2 swap chitin and cellulose. Animalia have no cell wall at all.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the wall materials of fungi and plants.
solution.time_saving_tip: Remember the link: fungi go with chitin, plants with cellulose and animals with no wall.

questions.question: Which set of entities is NOT placed in any kingdom of Whittaker's five-kingdom classification?

solution.key_concept: Viruses, viroids, prions and lichens are excluded from the five kingdoms.
steps: Bacteria, Mycoplasma and cyanobacteria belong to Monera.
Diatoms, slime moulds and protozoans belong to Protista.
Yeast, Penicillium and Agaricus belong to Fungi.
Viruses, viroids and lichens are not placed in any of the five kingdoms.
solution.why_not_others: Every other set belongs to Monera, Protista or Fungi.
solution.common_trap: Thinking that lichens go in Fungi or Plantae.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: In the five-kingdom classification, Chlamydomonas and Paramoecium are placed together in Kingdom Protista.
statements.R: Monera is the only kingdom of the five-kingdom system that contains prokaryotic organisms.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Protista groups unicellular eukaryotes, while Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom.
steps: Protista brings together Chlamydomonas, Chlorella, Paramoecium and Amoeba, so A is true.
Monera is the only prokaryotic kingdom, so R is true.
A is explained by both organisms being unicellular eukaryotes, not by Monera being prokaryotic.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, which rules out options 3 and 4. R does not explain why these two organisms are grouped together, which rules out option 1.
solution.common_trap: Choosing option 1 just because both statements are true and sound related.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: The two-kingdom system of Linnaeus successfully separated prokaryotes from eukaryotes but failed to separate unicellular from multicellular organisms.
statements.II: In the five-kingdom system, members of Kingdom Fungi show holozoic nutrition and have cell walls made of cellulose.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Shortcomings of the two-kingdom system and the defining features of fungi.
steps: The two-kingdom system failed to separate prokaryotes from eukaryotes. It also failed to separate unicellular from multicellular organisms. So I is incorrect.
Fungi are heterotrophic and absorptive, and their walls are made of chitin. Holozoic nutrition belongs to animals. So II is incorrect.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
solution.why_not_others: Each statement contains a false element, so no option that calls either statement correct can hold.
solution.common_trap: Accepting Statement I because its second half is true.

questions.question: Which organisms lack a cell wall, are the smallest living cells known and can survive without oxygen?

solution.key_concept: Mycoplasma are wall-less monerans.
steps: Mycoplasma lack a cell wall.
They are the smallest living cells and can survive without oxygen.
solution.why_not_others: Nostoc and Anabaena are cyanobacteria with a rigid wall. Methanogens are archaebacteria, which have a distinct cell wall.
solution.common_trap: Picking methanogens because they live without oxygen.

questions.question: Red tides in the sea are caused by:

solution.key_concept: Gonyaulax, a dinoflagellate, causes red tides.
steps: Dinoflagellates have two flagella and cellulose plates.
Rapid multiplication of Gonyaulax makes the sea appear red.
solution.why_not_others: Euglena does not cause red tides. Diatoms are chief producers in the oceans. Cyanobacteria form blooms, but these are not red tides.
solution.common_trap: Confusing cyanobacterial blooms with red tides.

questions.question: In which two classes of fungi does a dikaryotic (n+n) stage intervene between plasmogamy and karyogamy?

solution.key_concept: A dikaryophase occurs in Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes.
steps: Sexual reproduction in fungi follows the sequence plasmogamy, then karyogamy, then meiosis.
In Ascomycetes and Basidiomycetes, an n+n dikaryotic stage occurs between plasmogamy and karyogamy.
solution.why_not_others: Deuteromycetes have only an asexual phase. Phycomycetes do not show this dikaryotic stage.
solution.common_trap: Including Deuteromycetes, which have no sexual stage at all.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

solution.key_concept: Each class of fungi has typical example genera.
steps: Albugo belongs to Phycomycetes, so A-II.
Neurospora belongs to Ascomycetes, so B-IV.
Puccinia (rust) belongs to Basidiomycetes, so C-I.
Trichoderma belongs to Deuteromycetes, so D-III.
solution.why_not_others: Option 2 swaps the Ascomycete and Basidiomycete examples. Option 3 places Neurospora in Phycomycetes. Option 4 swaps Puccinia and Trichoderma.
solution.common_trap: Placing the rust fungus Puccinia in Deuteromycetes.
solution.time_saving_tip: Fixing Albugo as a phycomycete leaves only options 1, 2 and 4. Fixing Neurospora as an ascomycete then leaves options 1 and 4.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about Monera, Protista and Fungi are correct?

statements.A: Methanogens live in the gut of ruminants and produce methane in biogas.
statements.B: Euglenoids have a rigid cellulose cell wall.
statements.C: Chrysophytes have silica walls that form diatomaceous earth.
statements.D: Spores of slime moulds lack true walls and are easily destroyed.
statements.E: Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores and form basidiospores.

solution.key_concept: Salient features of monerans, protists and fungi.
steps: A is correct: methanogens live in the ruminant gut and produce methane.
B is wrong: euglenoids have a protein-rich pellicle, not a cell wall.
C is correct: chrysophyte silica walls form diatomaceous earth.
D is wrong: slime mould spores have true walls and are extremely resistant.
E is correct: Basidiomycetes lack asexual spores and form basidiospores.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): A, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 2 and 3 contain the false statements B or D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Assuming euglenoids have a cell wall because they photosynthesise like plants.

questions.question: The fungal component of a lichen is known as:

solution.key_concept: A lichen consists of a phycobiont (alga) and a mycobiont (fungus).
steps: The algal partner is the phycobiont.
The fungal partner is the mycobiont.
solution.why_not_others: The phycobiont is the alga. Mycorrhiza is a fungus and root association. Mycelium is a mass of hyphae.
solution.common_trap: Confusing mycobiont with mycorrhiza.

questions.question: Lichens are good indicators of air pollution because they do not grow in areas with high levels of:

solution.key_concept: Lichens are absent where $SO_2$ pollution is high.
steps: Lichens are sensitive to pollution.
They are especially absent in areas with high $SO_2$.
solution.why_not_others: $CO_2$, $N_2$ and $O_2$ are normal components of air.
solution.common_trap: Picking $CO_2$ because it is often linked with pollution.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes the roles of the partners in a lichen?
options: The fungus prepares food, while the alga absorbs water and minerals
The alga prepares food, while the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals
Both partners are autotrophic and share food equally
The alga provides shelter, while the fungus prepares food

solution.key_concept: Lichens show mutualism between an autotrophic alga and a fungus.
steps: The phycobiont (alga) is autotrophic and prepares food.
The mycobiont (fungus) provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): The alga prepares food, while the fungus provides shelter and absorbs water and minerals
solution.why_not_others: Fungi are heterotrophic, so they cannot prepare food. This rules out options 1, 3 and 4.
solution.common_trap: Reversing the roles of the two partners.

questions.question: Given below are two statements: Assertion A and Reason R. Choose the correct answer.

statements.A: Lichens are very good indicators of air pollution.
statements.R: Lichens act as pioneers on bare rock during primary succession.

options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true

solution.key_concept: Lichens indicate pollution and also act as pioneer organisms.
steps: Lichens do not grow in polluted, $SO_2$-rich areas, so A is true.
Lichens are pioneers on bare rock, so R is true.
Being a pioneer does not explain sensitivity to pollution.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
solution.why_not_others: Both statements are true, so options 3 and 4 are out. R gives no reason for pollution sensitivity, so option 1 is out.
solution.common_trap: Linking two true facts about lichens as cause and effect.

questions.question: Given below are two statements. Choose the most appropriate answer.

statements.I: In a lichen, the association between the alga and the fungus is so close that the lichen looks like a single organism.
statements.II: The association between a fungus and the roots of Pinus is a mycorrhiza and not a lichen.

options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

solution.key_concept: Lichen versus mycorrhiza.
steps: The lichen association is so close that it appears as one organism, so I is correct.
Mycorrhiza is a fungus and higher plant root association, as in Pinus, so II is correct.
solution.final_answer: Option (1): Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
solution.why_not_others: Both statements match the facts, so no option marking either as incorrect holds.
solution.common_trap: Calling the fungus and Pinus root association a lichen.

questions.question: Viroids, the cause of potato spindle tuber disease, were discovered by:

solution.key_concept: T.O. Diener discovered viroids in 1971.
steps: Diener identified free infectious RNA as the cause of potato spindle tuber disease.
solution.why_not_others: Ivanowsky studied the tobacco mosaic agent. Stanley crystallised viruses. Beijerinck coined the term contagium vivum fluidum.
solution.common_trap: Mixing up the scientists in the history of virology.

questions.question: Bacteriophages usually contain which type of genetic material?

solution.key_concept: Plant viruses usually have ssRNA, while bacteriophages usually have dsDNA.
steps: A virus has either DNA or RNA, never both.
Bacteriophages usually carry double-stranded DNA.
solution.why_not_others: Single-stranded RNA is typical of plant viruses. The other two options do not describe bacteriophages.
solution.common_trap: Applying the plant virus pattern (ssRNA) to bacteriophages.

questions.question: The causal agent of potato spindle tuber disease is:
options: An abnormally folded protein without nucleic acid
DNA enclosed in a protein capsid
A bacterium lacking a cell wall
Free RNA of low molecular weight lacking a protein coat

solution.key_concept: Viroids are free RNA molecules without a protein coat.
steps: Potato spindle tuber disease is caused by a viroid.
A viroid is free, low molecular weight RNA with no capsid.
solution.final_answer: Option (4): Free RNA of low molecular weight lacking a protein coat
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 describes prions. Option 2 describes a virus. Option 3 describes Mycoplasma.
solution.common_trap: Confusing viroids with prions.

questions.question: Match List-I with List-II and choose the correct answer.

list_II.label: I
list_II.text: Showed that viruses could be crystallised

list_II.label: III
list_II.text: Coined the term contagium vivum fluidum

list_II.label: IV
list_II.text: Found that the tobacco mosaic agent is smaller than bacteria

solution.key_concept: Key scientists in the history of virology.
steps: Ivanowsky (1892) found the tobacco mosaic agent is smaller than bacteria, so A-IV.
Beijerinck coined contagium vivum fluidum, so B-III.
Stanley crystallised viruses, so C-I.
Diener discovered viroids, so D-II.
solution.why_not_others: Option 1 swaps Ivanowsky and Beijerinck. Option 2 swaps Beijerinck and Stanley. Option 3 swaps Stanley and Diener.
solution.common_trap: Swapping the contributions of Ivanowsky and Beijerinck.
solution.time_saving_tip: D-II (Diener and viroids) rules out option 3 straight away.

questions.question: Which of the following statements about viruses, viroids and prions are correct?

statements.A: A virus contains both DNA and RNA enclosed in a capsid.
statements.B: Viruses are inert outside a host cell and are obligate parasites.
statements.C: Prions are abnormally folded proteins that cause BSE and Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease.
statements.D: Viroids have a protein coat and are larger than viruses.
statements.E: Mosaic formation, leaf rolling and vein clearing are symptoms of viral diseases in plants.

solution.key_concept: Distinguishing features of viruses, viroids and prions.
steps: A is wrong: a virus has either DNA or RNA, never both.
B is correct: viruses are inert outside a host and are obligate parasites.
C is correct: prions are misfolded proteins that cause BSE and CJD.
D is wrong: viroids lack a protein coat and are smaller than viruses.
E is correct: these are listed symptoms of viral disease in plants.
solution.final_answer: Option (2): B, C and E only
solution.why_not_others: Options 3 and 4 include the false statements A or D. Option 1 leaves out the true statement E.
solution.common_trap: Believing viroids have a capsid like viruses.
